title: Announcing The Forrester Wave™: Marketplace Platforms For Digital Services, Q4 2026
summary: The transaction is only one moment in the buying experience. Our latest Forrester Wave™ shows how marketplace platforms are evolving to orchestrate what happens around it.
body_markdown:
## Marketplaces Are The Operating Systems For The Buying Experience


It can seem like everything is becoming an operating system these days. There’s a business reason for it. Enterprises need more of their operations to run autonomously as complexity and scale increase. Your marketplace will need the same: enough automation to coordinate a growing ecosystem without increasing cost and headcount.


The transaction is only one moment in the buying experience that your marketplace must support. End buyers need to discover the right solution, understand its commercial terms, and put it to use as their needs evolve. Aspiring marketplace operators like you must coordinate the ecosystem behind that experience.


Your job is getting harder as what gets sold expands from software and services to AI agents and agent-powered outcomes. Your technology foundation now must sustain the buying experience around the transaction, not just process the transaction itself.


## What We Evaluated


For this Forrester Wave™, we evaluated the 10 most significant vendors capable of powering your branded marketplace: Amazon Web Services, Amdocs, AppDirect, Arrow Electronics, Beyond Now, CloudBlue, Comviva, In Time Tec, LotusFlare, and Pax8.


We found that marketplace platforms are becoming commerce orchestration platforms. Digital commerce still depends on coordinating products, participants, and transactions. Commerce orchestration goes further by connecting that work across your ecosystem so that end buyers can discover, buy, and use digital services as one buying experience.


**Here are three things you should do when selecting the technology foundation for your marketplace program:**


- **Don’t mistake programmability for orchestration.** Determine whether a vendor makes the complete marketplace process work or gives your organization the components to construct it. Marketplace platforms increasingly expose building blocks for sophisticated digital commerce. You see the difference when your buying experience spans multiple suppliers, systems, and commercial relationships. Stronger orchestration coordinates those dependencies across organizational boundaries, while other approaches leave more of that work to your integrations and processes.
- **Make marketplace intelligence actionable.** Determine whether the platform turns what it learns about your marketplace into better decisions and automated workflows. Analytics can show you what is happening; the more valuable capability is connecting marketplace signals to what happens next.
- **Preserve room for agentic commerce.** Evaluate whether the platform can accommodate agents as governed participants *as well as* commercial offerings as those business models mature. AI agents are arriving faster than the commercial models needed to govern and monetize them. Vendors can already apply AI to marketplace workflows, and some are beginning to commercialize agents themselves. Governance, orchestration, and monetization remain works in progress.
